items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I returned to London in October for a festival at the Hammersmith Theatre and blew this one with Alex Welsch

ctx.x: Ben eventually arrived and we did some original numbers and one that I composed in the studio and called it "Pound Horn", because I had learned that studio trumpettists that doubled on flugel horn were paid an extra pound when the horn was used at a session and English musicians called it a pound horn.

Ben did some numbers alone with the rhythm section. There was one number that I would loved to have re-recorded, which was 'Satin Doll', but Jack Higgins insisted that some unknown girl singer he wanted to push perhaps, record a number and that did not leave time enough to do anything more. We had recorded the album between 9 a.m. and 1 p.m. The rhythm section had a T.V. date with Alex Welsch and could not stay any longer. I was not very satisfied with the "Satin Doll" version I did record.

The next day I played the 100 club and Nottingham the 29th. Replaced Buck with the John Chilton Swing Kings at a place called 'Dog and Fox' in Wimbledon, the 30th. Here was another surprise for me when I learned that John Chilton was a musician and a trumpet player to boot. When I did my first tour in England, John was collaborating with Jim Godbolt in the booking agency business. We had quite a few get togethers, but he never spoke about being a trumpet man or even a musician. And no one else ever mentioned it…
